description.narrative: The objective of the AF is to improve inclusiveness of school funding management and enhance support to teachersa?? professional development while increasing transition rates of poor and at-risk students.

The objective of the Decentralizing Funding to Schools Project is to help improve and expand Myanmar's School Grants Program and Student Stipends Program. There are three components to the project, the first component being expansion and improvement of the school grants program. All schools with primary students currently supported by government budget funding are eligible for participation in the school grants program. Expansion of the program, therefore, will mean increasing the size of annual operating grants to schools from approximately US$250, US$400 and US$500 per school for small, medium and large schools, respectively, to targets of US$900, US$1,200 and US$1,800 per school, respectively, over a four year period. The second component is the expansion and improvement of the student stipends program. While all government-supported schools in Myanmar are nominally eligible to participate in the existing student stipends program, the small size of the program (11,000 stipends to be awarded nationwide) effectively means that, while most schools apply for stipends funding, few schools are actually selected to participate in the program and those that do participate would have, in most cases, no more than two stipend students. Finally, the third component is the capacity improvement to strengthen monitoring and implementation of programs. This project will focus on training, and on conducting a baseline assessment of early grade reading. On training, Ministry of Education, or MoE will design and begin implementing a national training program during school year 2014-15 aimed at introducing the new school grants and stipends program to township officials and school headmasters.

title.narrative: 4. Townships having transferred funds to at least 80 percent of their schools, in accordance with latest SISP guidelines (DLIs 5, 8, 11, 17, and 21)

comment.narrative:
<p>DFSP original target 200 townships was overachieved at 115.5% as DLI (11) was verified by third party monitoring as 231 townships (Cardno Y1 report dated 30 April 2018).</p>
<p>For the Additional Financing Revised target 280 townships, it was 100% achieved verified by third party monitoring as 330 townships transferred funds to 99.1 % of their schools in accordance with SISP guidelines. (Cardno Y6 Report, DLI 17) </p>

<p>DFSP original target was fully achieved. The guidelines for School Improvement Support program (SISP) and Student Stipends program (SSP) were developed and endorsed by MoE in 2014-2015 SY. Based on the lessons learned from project year one implementation, the guidelines were revised in 2015-2016 and 2016-2017 respectively. </p>

<p>For the Additional Financing, both SISP and SSP guidelines were revised again in 2018-2019 SY to include social inclusion, community consultations, complaint mechanism, and BMY specific approach in the SISP and SSP.</p>

<p>The operational guideline for AF new component, 'Teacher Mentoring and School Cluster Support program', and 'Mentoring Handbook' were developed and endorsed by MoE in 2017-2018 SYand refined in 2018-2019 SY.</p>

<p>The teachers' guide for Early Grade Reading Intervention Pilot (EGRI) was developed in 2018-2019 SY. The operational guideline was developed in 2019-2020. </p>

<p>This indicator was fully achieved.</p>

title.narrative: 12. Township education officials trained in implementing programs in accordance with the latest guidelines (non-cumulative).
6. Schools that have a school improvement plan (DLI12)

comment.narrative:
<p>DFSP original target was overachieved at 99.1% in 2018, verified by third party monitoring (Cardno Y1 DLI verification report, verified DLI 12 (30 April 2018).</p>
<p>The AF Revised target was achieved at 99%. But there was a slight shortfall all at 89.7%, according to M&E QA report (Y6 Cardno QA report 30 April 2020). The shortfall was due to the time of data collection that took place in June, the first month of the school year and the actual percentage was increased to 99% by the end of the school year. </p>

<p>This indicator was fully achieved. The Student Stipends program operational guideline was first developed when the project came into effective in 2014 and revised two times during later years based on the process monitoring findings. </p>

title.narrative: 11. School heads trained in implementing programs, in accordance with the latest guidelines (non-cumulative)

comment.narrative:
<p>DFSP original target was 160% overachieved as 48,010 SHs trained (MoE Status report 2017-2018) because school grants program was expanded to all Middle and High schools, and Monastic schools in country. After year one implementation, MoE decided to expand the school grants provision to middle, high and monastic schools, not just limited to primary level.</p>
<p>For AF target, it was 99% achieved (MoE Status report 2019-2020 SY).</p>

title.narrative: 9. Students having received stipends payment in accordance with the latest SSP guidelines (DLIs 4, 7, 10, 17, and 21)

comment.narrative:
<p>DFSP original target of stipend payment to 100,000 students in 2018 was overachieved at 151,175 (151%). This indicator was verified by third party monitoring (DLI Verification report, May 2019). </p>
<p>AF revised target of 250,000 students was overachieved as 305,503 students in 2019-2020 at 122% based on MoE admin data. The number of stipend students was based on 2019-20 school year total (244,331) and added with the number of Grade 11 stipend students (61,172) who left the basic education system after Grade 11in 2014-2015, 2015-2016, 2016-2017, 2017-2018 and 2018-2019 school years. The number were 2,130, 7,322, 14,305, 18,811, and 18,604 respectively.</p>
